To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

specific sulfation patterns in combination with certain types of glycosylation are the structural motifs responsible for the antico-agulation of marine carbohydrates, and that the anticoagulants are not only heparins, but also marine polysaccharides.
the anticoagulating activity of marine glycans is based on the presence of sulfated fucose, sulfated galactose, sulfated iduronic acid and 4-sulfated glucosamine units.
sulfation and glycan structures of marine glycans play a key role in the anticoagulants activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the anticoagulants of marine organisms.
the identification of structural motifs that are responsible for the antico-agulant properties of marine polysaccharides.
the elucidation of the structure-activity relationships of marine sulfated polysac-charides, with special emphasis on their anticoagulant properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

specific combinations of sulfated and non-sulfated units in the backbones of marine polysaccharides and specific sulfation patterns at certain glycosyl residues are the structural requirements for their anticoagulant properties.
sulfation and glyco-structures are the structural requirements for the antico-agulant activity of marine polysaccharides.
the specific combinations of sulfated and glycosylated residues are key structural players for anticoagulation in certain marine glycans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sulfated polysac-charides from marine organisms are the most potent anticoagulants found to date, and the anticoagulatory activities are dependent on the structural combinations of sulfation and glyco-configuration.
the sulfation patterns and the glycosylation types are the key structural requirements for the antico-agulant activity of marine glycans.
sulfation is the key structural player for anticoagulation and the glycosylation pattern is an important structural parameter for this activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sulfation and glycan types are the main structural determinants for anticoagulation.
the anticoagulants are not the only biological activities of marine polysaccharides.
specific sulfation patterns and/or glycosylation types, combined in the same molecule, are key structural requirements for the antico-agulant activities of marine glycans.
